The big picture: I've been in technology a long time. I take these threats seriously , but I'm not in panic mode. When something breaks, we need to understand what happened, how far it reaches and what we can do about it. A frightening headline doesn't answer those questions. Zoom out: The way I think about it, we've put powerful tools in more hands, and people are taking potshots to see what they can hit. Those shots can do real damage, and we need to protect ourselves. items.summary: Anthropic will make its Wall Street debut Thursday at a moment of profound contradiction in the history of AI: The humans are embattled — bogged down by scandal, financial turmoil and political revolt. But the machines are ascendant — accelerating toward an "intelligence explosion" they expect will transform civilization. Why it matters: The industry's recent chaos has obscured a breathtaking surge in technological progress, forcing some of the world's leading researchers to reconsider just how soon AI could surpass human intelligence. Zoom in: Inside Anthropic, soon to be valued north of $1 trillion, independent researchers at METR found that AI models are advancing at nearly twice their historical pace — largely fueled, they believe, by AI itself. items.title: Exclusive: Bots amplified conspiracy theories and panic about recent tech outages
items.summary: Bot accounts have helped spread conspiracy theories about a wave of major tech outages over the last week, according to new research shared exclusively with Axios. Why it matters: Purveyors of disinformation appear to be exploiting public anxiety over the cyberattacks and fragile infrastructure, amplifying suspicions of coordinated cyberattacks and government cover-ups. While it's unclear who's behind these accounts, the pattern shows that when technology failures lack substantive explanations, bot networks will fill the void to manufacture panic. Catch up quick: Microsoft, Apple, JPMorgan Chase, United, Workday, the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Security Agency each faced outages over the last week. Then came the conspiracy theories: When the FAA grounded flights for four hours Friday, people were quick to assume it was tied to the rollout of an AI tool at the agency.

Atoms in sync: Superradiance offers a new kind of frequency comb
items.summary: When scientists shine a laser beam into a crystal, they typically expect a steady glow as the crystal's atoms are energized and begin to emit light. But in early 2024, while searching for something else entirely, researchers in the lab of Caltech's Andrei Faraon saw a crystal flash in a regular rhythm, like a metronome keeping a beat. The flashes came from billions of atoms embedded in the crystal. Coupled to a tiny superconducting circuit, the atoms had become synchronized and started emitting light together through a special quantum phenomenon known as superradiance.

The Advertising Standards Authority says the adverts by online healthcare provider Voy made misleading claims. Five adverts by online healthcare provider Voy have been banned by the watchdog for making misleading claims linked to low testosterone in men. It said they were misleading as they linked common symptoms such as irritability and fatigue to low testosterone. Voy said it had withdrawn the adverts while the investigation was under way and would not run them again. The NHS says that while testosterone levels in men fall as they age, this is "unlikely" to cause any problems in itself.

The Amazon CEO said he was originally "biased against" Pattinson "because he's already so famous". Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has said he was "heavily involved" in picking actor Robert Pattinson for the role of James Bond in the next 007 film. Speaking onstage at an event in California, the Amazon CEO said he was originally "biased against" Pattinson - who starred in a number of blockbuster films including Batman and the Twilight franchise - "because he's already so famous". Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey - who helped the Gunners win the Double in 1970-71 - has died at the age of 81. Tiger Woods will return to golf at the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas next month, his first 72-hole tournament since 2024. The 15-time major champion's last appearance in a PGA Tour event was at the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon, where he missed the cut . Prior to that, he completed the 2024 Masters, finishing in 60th place. Woods then missed the entire 2025 season due to a ruptured left Achilles tendon suffered while training for the Masters. The Hero World Challenge is an invitational tournament hosted by Woods himself, featuring a select field of 20 players. The 72-hole event has no cut, and participants are required to walk the course, as carts are not permitted.

The ancient human species appears to have been a keen traveler, too Ancient fossils reveal Homo erectus survived in China some 200,000 years longer than we thought The ancient human Homo erectus emerged nearly two million years ago and spread from Africa to as far as the Indonesian island of Java. Now fossils discovered in two caves in southern China are helping to color in parts of this ancient human ancestor’s journey. By analyzing the fossils, researchers have found that H. erectus survived on the Asian mainland for around 200,000 years longer than we previously thought. He then signaled for Rashid Shaheed to pick up the football, as he'd stepped out of bounds, to prevent an illegal touch.

Former Chicago Tribune sportswriter Fred Mitchell, 78, died Tuesday after a battle with leukemia, his family announced. Mitchell spent more than four decades at the Chicago Tribune, He started at the Tribune in 1974, becoming the first African American sportswriter at the Tribune. At the Tribune, Mitchell served as a beat writer for the Chicago Bulls, Cubs and Bears before becoming a columnist. After retiring from the Tribune, he went on to serve as an adjunct professor at Northwestern University and DePaul University.

Jamal Anderson was the last NFL running back to amass 500+ touches in a season, including the playoffs. That was in 1998. Jahmyr Gibbs could join him. Only four running backs have collected 500+ touches. Emmitt Smith did it twice: 516 in 1992 and then 519 in 1995. Anderson had 517 in 1998. Terrell Davis holds the record with 531 in 1997. Notice that all of this happened within a six-year timeframe... and no one's done it since, even though the league expanded the playoffs and extended the regular season by a game. In fact, no RB has topped 433 touches since DeMarco Murray posted 497 in 2014. Murray regressed sharply the following season. That's usually what happens.

The Steelers haven't won a road game against the Eagles in Philadelphia since 1965. Here's how the 11-game drought unfolded. The Pittsburgh Steelers have a long history with the Philadelphia Eagles, but their trips across the state line have been anything but successful in recent decades. Pittsburgh has lost 11 consecutive road games against Philadelphia, dating back to 1966. The Steelers' last victory in the City of Brotherly Love came on Oct. 24, 1965, when they defeated the Eagles 20-14 at Franklin Field. More than six decades later, the drought has stretched across three stadiums, multiple generations of players and several eras of Steelers football.

No state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide. When the judges of the International Court of Justice read out their verdict in the seven-year-old genocide case filed by The Gambia against Myanmar on Thursday, they could make history. In the years since the Genocide Convention was signed in 1948, after the Nazi Holocaust, dozens of individuals have been successfully prosecuted for the crime of genocide, in conflicts such as those in Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia. But no state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide.

India will remain predominantly Hindu, though its Muslim population is projected to grow faster, according to a new survey. India will remain overwhelmingly Hindu for decades to come, but its religious composition is projected to shift gradually. A new study by the Pew Research Center, projecting the world's religious populations to 2070, estimates that Hindus will make up 76% of India's population by then, down from 79% in 2020, while the Muslim share will rise from 15% to 20%. The shift is rooted largely in differences in age and fertility: Indian Muslims are younger than Hindus and, on average, have more children.

The proposed Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill will also include capping ground rent at £250. The government is to introduce new laws to scrap the way flats are built in England and Wales. Under the proposed bill, most new leasehold flats will be banned and replaced with commonhold, where residents collectively own and manage their buildings. Matthew Pennycook, the housing minister, said the current leasehold system was "blighting lives" and was an "anachronism in the twenty-first century". The legislation follows Labour's 2024 election manifesto to "bring the feudal leasehold system to an end" - with further details expected to be set out later.

A Tour putting coach reveals how eye alignment and a square face solve missed putts. Simple setup changes bring back confidence on the greens. The first error was eye placement. Sweeney noted that many players keep their eyes inside the ball line, closer to their feet. "Where your eyes are right now, I tend to see if players' eyes are inside the ball line; they tend to look out to the right," Sweeney said. This setup forces the putter to move on the inside during the backstroke. The result is a stroke path that goes from in to out, missing the hole to the right on short putts.

Allan Mulloy, a 15-year-old from Champion who lives with a rare disease, got to design cleats for the Browns' Jerry Jeudy to wear at an upcoming game. When he was 7 years old, Allan was diagnosed with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), a rare genetic muscle condition that eventually leads to losing the ability to walk. It also affects breathing muscles, the heart and life expectancy, said Dr. Matthew Ginsberg , pediatric neurologist with Akron Children's Hospital . Today, Allan uses a power chair to get around, but he isn't in a chair full time, as he can still walk short distances. When other kids ask him about his condition, he tells them what he can do instead of what he can't.

Deirdre Keane had already run more than 60 marathons when she decided to take on a new challenge of completing the World Marathon Majors. She just didn’t expect to be running them while pregnant. Earlier this month, the 38-year-old nurse practitioner and management consultant ran the New York City Marathon – her hometown race – in her third trimester. It was the seventh marathon she had finished while pregnant and was the final race she needed to achieve her goal of running all the World Marathon Majors in the same year.
